title: Skills and Workforce Development Agency Bill
what_it_is: Skills and Workforce Development Agency Bill

sections.label: SSG-supported training participation growth
sections.summary: Participants in SSG-supported training grew from 418,000 in 2016 to more than 600,000 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The number of individuals participating in SSG-supported training each year has grown from 418,000 in 2016 to more than 600,000 in 2025.

sections.label: WSG-assisted individuals tripled
sections.summary: Individuals assisted by WSG and its partners tripled from 127,000 in 2017 to 355,000 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The number of individuals assisted by WSG and its partners has tripled from 127,000 in 2017 to 355,000 in 2025.

sections.label: Singapore ageing population threshold
sections.summary: Singapore citizens aged 65 and above rose from about one in eight in 2015 to more than one in five today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In 2015, roughly one in eight Singapore citizens was aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Today, it is more than one in five, crossing the threshold of a super-aged society.

sections.label: Merging SSG and WSG
sections.summary: SSG and WSG are being brought together into a single upgraded engine for skills and workforce development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To stay ahead of change, we must therefore be able to continuously adapt with the times as well as with new realities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: That is why we are bringing SSG and WSG together, combining the strengths that both agencies have built up over the past decade into a single upgraded engine for skills and workforce development, ready to support Singaporeans and employers to navigate an age of unprecedented change.

sections.label: Career Kaki AI advisor
sections.summary: With GovTech, an AI advisor called Career Kaki was rolled out as a personal digital concierge for careers and skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In partnership with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech), we have rolled out an AI advisor called Career Kaki that serves as a personal digital concierge for careers and skills, available at any time of the day to help those who are unsure of their next steps.

sections.label: Free premium AI tools
sections.summary: At Budget 2026, the Prime Minister announced free access to premium AI tools for those taking selected training courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At Budget 2026, the Prime Minister announced the latest addition to SWDA's offering – free access to premium AI tools for those who take up selected training courses.

sections.label: Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package
sections.summary: SWDA will integrate SSG and WSG workforce transformation schemes in a digital portal, with the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant and redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Through the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package, SWDA will bring together workforce transformation schemes from SSG and WSG in an integrated enterprise digital portal to support holistic workforce transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The recently implemented SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant (Job Redesign+), is a key resource that employers can tap on to redesign job roles, build internal capabilities and adopt workforce tech solutions for workforce transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the second half of this year, employers will be able to invest in workforce development with greater ease through the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

sections.label: Nine pilots for under-served groups
sections.summary: Nine pilots are underway testing models for under-served groups including fresh graduates, families with complex needs and those returning to the labour force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Nine pilots are already underway, testing innovative models targeting under-served groups, including fresh graduates, families with complex needs and those returning to the labour force after a period of absence.

sections.label: SWDA Bill tabled
sections.summary: The SWDA Bill has been tabled to give effect to these measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To give effect to them, we have tabled the SWDA Bill.

sections.label: SWDA functions
sections.summary: SWDA's functions will cover existing SSG and WSG functions and extend to promoting career and employment services and training in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: SWDA's functions will cover the existing functions of SSG and WSG, and extend them to include promoting the development of career and employment services and training in Singapore.

sections.label: Transfer of WSG and SSG employees
sections.summary: WSG and SSG employees will be transferred to SWDA on terms no less favourable than their present ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Employees of WSG and SSG will be transferred to SWDA on terms that are no less favourable than their present ones.

sections.label: Repeal of SSG and WSG Acts
sections.summary: Parts 10 and 11 repeal the SSG Act and WSG Act, make related amendments, and set out the framework to establish SWDA in the third quarter of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Parts 10 and 11 repeal the SSG Act and the WSG Act and make consequential and related amendments to other Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The establishment of the Workforce Development Agency in 2003, its subsequent restructuring into SSG and WSG in 2016, and now the creation of SWDA reflect the same underlying commitment: to invest in our people and to ensure that our institutions remain best positioned to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Bill presented today sets out the legislative framework to establish the SWDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: If the Bill is passed, SWDA will be established in the third quarter of 2026 as a cornerstone in answering our workforce challenges in the decade ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It will support every Singaporean across a career that may be long, multi-staged, varied and non-linear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It will help employers navigate transformation and meet their workforce needs with greater confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It will bring coherence and quality to the full ecosystem of career and employment services and training that our workers and businesses can depend on.

sections.label: SSG and WSG established
sections.summary: Ten years ago, SSG and WSG were established and reconstituted, one focused on skills and the other on jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Ten years ago, we established SSG and reconstituted WSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: One focused on skills, the other on jobs.

sections.label: AI shortens skills half-life
sections.summary: AI is shortening the half-life of skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: At the same time, AI is shortening the half-life of skills.

sections.label: SWDA formation strategic reset
sections.summary: The formation of the SWDA is a strategic reset bringing skills and careers into one continuous journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The formation of the SWDA is a strategic reset, bringing skills and careers into one continuous journey.

sections.label: FairPrice Store of Tomorrow visit
sections.summary: The second visit was to FairPrice's Store of Tomorrow at Punggol Coast Mall, Singapore's first generative-AI-powered supermarket.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Our second visit took us to FairPrice's Store of Tomorrow at Punggol Coast Mall – Singapore's first generative-AI-powered supermarket.

sections.label: AV allowances for trained workers
sections.summary: Workers trained to operate autonomous equipment now receive AV allowances, recognising their higher skills and responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Workers trained to operate autonomous equipment now receive AV allowances, recognising their higher skills and responsibilities they carry.

sections.label: SSG and WSG merger bold steps
sections.summary: The merger of SSG and WSG must lead to bold steps to streamline delivery, simplify administration, and centre worker and employer outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The merger of SSG and WSG must lead to bold steps, not incremental ones, to streamline programme delivery, simplify grant and funding administration, and take a genuinely customer-centric approach that puts real worker and employer outcomes right at the centre.

sections.label: Caregiver return-to-work pathway
sections.summary: SWDA would give Joanne a return-to-work pathway bundling caregiver respite support, a training allowance and a CPF top-up, with close to 1,000 CUBbies since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If SWDA gets this right, Joanne would be supported by a structured return-to-work pathway for caregivers – one that bundles caregiver respite support to free her time for training, a training allowance to sustain her through the programme and a CPF top-up in her first month back at work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Since we launched it in 2023, we have close to 1,000 CUBbies in the programme, and in 2025, we expanded it to professional, manager and executive (PME) roles, including accounting and office administration.

sections.label: Fatigue monitoring and job redesign
sections.summary: SWDA would use AI-informed fatigue monitoring and job redesign to give Sakthi a smarter shift structure that keeps him and his passengers safe.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If SWDA gets this right, AI-informed fatigue monitoring and job redesign can enable Sakthi to work a smarter shift structure, one that is informed by data about when fatigue peaks, that keeps him safe, keeps his passengers safe and keeps him economically active and contributing for longer.

sections.label: Platform driver fears autonomous vehicles
sections.summary: A platform driver of two years, reading about autonomous vehicles, asks what will become of him and wants to reskill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: While he searched for work, he turned to platform driving to keep his family afloat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: But now, two years in, he reads the news about autonomous vehicles (AVs) and he comes to me with a question that I have heard more than once: "Ms Yeo, if the technology matures, what will belong of me?" He wants to reskill.

sections.label: David's gradual reskilling transition
sections.summary: SWDA would give David structured financial support to drive part-time while undertaking a credentialled reskilling programme connected to employment pipelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If SWDA gets it right, David would have the access to structured financial support that allows him to transition gradually, to drive part-time while undertaking a credentialled reskilling programme connected to real employment pipelines in sectors where his original IT background, will open doors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: They sit across from me at kopi chit-chats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: They are the reason this Bill matters, and the reason I hope we will measure SWDA's success not just by the programmes launched or grants disbursed, but by the number of real Singaporeans whose working lives genuinely change for the better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement stands ready and our unions, our Tripartite Jobs Council will continue to walk the ground and we will hold SWDA and ourselves to the standard of making transformation inclusive, practical and human-centred.

sections.label: Reversing 2016 agency bifurcation
sections.summary: The Bill reverses the 2016 policy decision to split the then Workforce Development Agency into SSG and WSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill fundamentally reverses the 2016 policy decision to bifurcate the then Workforce Development Agency into SSG and WSG.

sections.label: Measuring merger success and KPIs
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government will measure the merger's success against the 2016 separation and what KPIs the new agency will use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How will the Government measure the success of this merger compared to the 2016 separation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Specifically, what key performance indicators (KPIs) will the new agency use to meaningfully tackle structural issues in labour mobility and skills development?

sections.label: Restructuring cost and rebranding budget
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to enumerate the restructuring cost, including rebranding, collateral updates and IT and payroll integration, and compare it with 2016 separation costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Minister enumerate the actual cost associated with this restructuring, including the budget set aside for rebranding efforts, the updating of physical and digital collateral as well as the integration of various IT and payroll systems, among other things, across the merging entities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share how this compare to the costs associated with separating these agencies in 2016?

sections.label: Aptitude-based admissions quotas expansion
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will encourage university and polytechnic admissions officers to further expand quotas for aptitude-based admissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To complement this early intervention, will the Government encourage university and polytechnic admissions officers to further expand their quotas for aptitude-based admissions?

sections.label: New agency ITM coordination with MTI
sections.summary: Asks how the new agency will coordinate with MTI to harmonise its ITMs with training curricula in real time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Minister explain how this new agency will coordinate work with MTI to ensure that it harmonises its ITMs with training curricula in real time?

sections.label: Merger performance indicators and training subsidies
sections.summary: Warns the merger risks reversal without published performance indicators, and proposes the proportion of public training subsidies going to courses with documented employment outcomes within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Without clear published performance indicators, this merger risks the same fate as the 2016 separation – celebrated at the inception, reversed a decade later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, the proportion of public training subsidies going to courses that yield documented employment outcomes within six months.

sections.label: Median time to employment indicators
sections.summary: Proposes median time to employment after SWDA-assisted job searches, broken down by age band, PMET status and service provider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, median time to employment following SWDA-assisted job searches, broken down by age band, professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) versus non-PMET status and by individual service providers.

sections.label: SWDA programme and scheme reviews
sections.summary: Asks if SWDA will consider an extended higher-value GRIT programme, review the JSS salary cap and criteria, and require responsible AI practices under Job Redesign+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Will SWDA consider launching an extended and higher-value iteration of the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) programme, with opportunities ranging from one to two years and with monthly traineeship allowances on par with starting salaries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As only over 3,000 involuntarily unemployed workers received at least one payout, out of the 10,000 SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme (JSS) applications received and despite 60,000 workers expected to be eligible for the scheme every year, will SWDA consider reviewing the scheme's salary cap, criteria for involuntary unemployment and service delivery experience?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Following the European Union, South Korea and Vietnam's introduction of AI legislation and explicit classification of employment-related AI as "high risk", will SWDA require responsible practices, such as anti-discrimination risk assessments, human oversight and right-to-know transparency, when deploying AI-enabled human resources technology under the Workforce Development Grant (Job Redesign+) programme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Measures have been recently rolled out to raise the quality of training providers seeking course approvals and funding, including requiring more practice hours and suspension for those with low ratings.

sections.label: Non-job-related learning quality
sections.summary: Defines high quality non-job-related learning as motivating further learning, and urges SWDA to review internship quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: For non-job-related learning for exploratory or personal interest reasons, high quality can be defined as learners motivated for further learning and future pursuits, as opposed to poor experiences becoming barriers to developing a mindset of lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I also encourage SWDA to review the quality of student internships as internship-stacking and credit-bearing internships become more commonplace, especially for non-university graduates whose starting salaries lag their university peers.

sections.label: Singapore workforce training investment
sections.summary: Singapore invested billions early in workforce and skills development, and over 60% of resident workers hold tertiary qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Unlike other countries, where unions need to lobby for fairer access to training opportunities and employment support, Singapore has invested billions into our workforce and skills development ecosystem, and earlier than most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We also have a highly educated workforce with over 60% of resident workers holding tertiary qualifications, and over 40% holding degrees.

sections.label: Training supply and labour demand disconnect
sections.summary: A disconnect between training supply and labour demand causes underused talent and mismatch, leading employers to hire externally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At the same time, a disconnect between training supply and labour demand results in underutilised talent and skills or qualifications mismatch, which drive employers to hire externally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In other words, we end up paying twice, once to train Singaporeans and again, to import foreign skills, while weakening the Singaporean Core.

sections.label: Funding tied to outcomes
sections.summary: Funding should be more closely tied to or conditional on quantitative or qualitative outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Moving forward, I submit that funding must be more closely tied to or even conditional upon outcomes, that is, whether quantitative, like time-to-placement, or qualitative, like more meaningful and autonomous tasks within work scope.

sections.label: Expanded underemployment definition
sections.summary: Recommends an expanded definition of underemployment and closer tracking of these trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This refers to when workers can work more hours or take on higher-skilled roles but are unable to or choose not to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We therefore recommend an expanded definition of underemployment and closer tracking of these trends.

sections.label: AI adoption training focus
sections.summary: Ministry of Manpower survey shows businesses adopting or intending to adopt AI focus more on training than job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The latest survey report released by the Ministry of Manpower shows that among businesses which have already adopted or intend to adopt AI, more are focused on training and skills upgrading rather than on redesigning jobs.

sections.label: AI adoption and job redesign
sections.summary: An MOM survey shows most Singapore companies have not adopted AI, and the member asks if the new agency will drive job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A recent MOM survey shows that the majority of Singapore companies have not adopted AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among the 28.5% that have begun using AI, meaningful integration remains limited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For companies that have started or plan to support the use of AI for employees, their focus remains overwhelmingly on training and upskilling and the provision of AI tools and subscriptions, rather than job redesign and career progression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If we invest in upskilling workers, but do not change what they come back to – the same job scope, the same workflow, plus a backlog of work and emails that accumulated while we were upskilling – then we have not transformed anything.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, I ask the Minister, will the new agency be resourced and empowered to drive job redesign at the scale that Singapore genuinely needs?

sections.label: Singapore skills-first hiring index
sections.summary: Singapore ranked 12 of 30 in the OECD-IAL skills-first index, and ranked last on employers not prioritising degrees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore ranked 12 out of 30 countries in the inaugural Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development-Institute for Adult Learning (OECD-IAL) Skills-First Readiness and Adoption Index published last year, where we fall short is not in worker willingness to upskill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Only 21% of Singapore employers saw removing degree requirements and adopting skills-first hiring as a promising way to increase talent availability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And when it comes to employers who would not prioritise a university degree when assessing candidates' skills, Singapore ranked last.

sections.label: Degree requirements increase
sections.summary: Degree requirements increased by 5.3% in the same period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Degree requirements increased by 5.3% in the same period.

sections.label: Public Service job posting tracking
sections.summary: The Public Service does not track job postings with formal academic requirements, and no direct answer came on skills-based hiring targets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The answer I received was that the Public Service, our largest employer "do not track the number of job postings that do or do not include formal academic requirements in their criteria." I also did not get a direct response to the second part of my question about target and timelines established to accelerate skills-based hiring across public agencies.

sections.label: Integration milestones and training safeguards
sections.summary: The member asks for key milestones and timelines for full integration and safeguards for individuals in training and job search.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What are the key milestones and expected timelines for full integration so that workers, employers and training providers know what to anticipate?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what safeguards will be in place to ensure that individuals currently in training and active job search continue training and receive uninterrupted career guidance and job matching support during this transition?

sections.label: New agency coordination and training formats
sections.summary: The member asks how the new agency will use coordination powers to intervene early and expand flexible training formats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how the new agency will use the coordination powers outlined in the Bill to intervene early in disrupted sectors to support workers before displacement occurs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How will the agency ensure that flexible training formats and blended learning pathways are expanded to support workers with irregular schedules and those with caregiving responsibilities?

sections.label: Support for younger workers
sections.summary: The passage asks how the new agency will support younger workers whose employment is disrupted by restructuring or who struggle to secure stable roles after contract work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how the new agency will support younger workers whose employment are disrupted by restructuring or who struggle to secure stable roles after completing contract work?

sections.label: Partnership and employer feedback
sections.summary: The passage seeks clarification on how the agency will work with industry players, associations, unions and sector partners, and how employer feedback will be incorporated into training pathways and programme design.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: He also spoke about the importance of partnership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, I would like seek clarification on how the agency will work with the various industry players, industry associations, unions and sector partners to ensure that the SMEs receive timely, practical and sector relevant support as they navigate the workforce transformation and adopt new practices on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How will the agency ensure that employer feedback is systematically incorporated into training pathways and programme design?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And will employers be engaged in curriculum design and workforce planning?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Consolidation alone does not guarantee a seamless experience for workers or employers, nor does it automatically ensure that the new agency will be able to proactively address technological disruptions or uphold the quality and effectiveness of training and support across all formats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: These outcomes will depend heavily on strong implementation, clear accountability for results and close partnership with employers, unions, industry associations and training providers.

sections.label: Coordinated skills-jobs system
sections.summary: The passage states the intention is to create a more coordinated system connecting skills to jobs and jobs back to skills in a continuous loop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The intention is to create a more coordinated system, one that connects skills to jobs and jobs back to skills in a continuous loop.

sections.label: Overlapping programme rules
sections.summary: The passage states that similar programmes such as WSG's Career Conversion Programmes and SSG's Career Transition Programmes operate with different rules, funding structures and employer touchpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similar programmes, such as WSG's Career Conversion Programmes and SSG's Career Transition Programmes, operate with different rules, funding structures and employer touchpoints.

sections.label: Rationalising overlapping schemes
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the agency will use the merger to rationalise and align overlapping schemes into a more coherent, employer-facing system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the agency use this merger to rationalise and align these overlapping schemes into a more coherent, employer-facing system so that a firm pursuing a single objective, such as redeployment or upskilling, does not have to operate across multiple tracks?

sections.label: Verification, inspection, funding recovery
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill introduces stronger powers around verification, inspection and recovery of funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces stronger powers around verification, inspection and recovery of funding.

sections.label: risk-based approach for agency
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the agency can move towards a more risk-based approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, can the agency move towards a more risk-based approach?

sections.label: applied firm-level capability training
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the agency will emphasise applied, firm-level capability so training links to measurable business outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, will the agency place greater emphasis on applied, firm-level capability so that training is more directly linked to measurable business outcomes?

sections.label: emphasis on rebound
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the agency will place stronger emphasis on what is called the rebound.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the agency place a stronger emphasis on what we may call the "rebound"?

sections.label: incentives for employer-led redeployment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the agency will consider strengthening incentives and support for employer-led redeployment to encourage companies to build and transition their existing workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the agency consider strengthening incentives and support for such employer-led redeployment, so that companies are encouraged to build and transition their existing workforce?

sections.label: transitional regulations and service charter
sections.summary: The passage states things should not be slowed or require rework due to changed administering structure, notes the Bill provides transitional regulations over two years, and asks about publishing a service charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These should not be slowed down or require rework simply because the administering structure has changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill provides for transitional regulations over a two-year period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would also like to ask whether the agency will consider publishing a service charter, setting out expected response times, processing timelines, escalating channels and sector points of contact.

sections.label: clarity on jobs skills pathways
sections.summary: The passage states the problem is clarity on growing jobs, skills, pathways and help, and that the Bill gives SWDA a broad remit across career, employment and training matters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The problem is whether the way forward is clear, whether there is clarity: in what jobs are growing,	what skills really matter, which pathway is worth taking and who can help me get there?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill gives SWDA a broad remit across career, employment and training matters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is meant to support students preparing for entry into the labour market, Singaporean's seeking employment or re-employment and employees seeking to develop their careers and remain in productive employment.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council and disruption
sections.summary: The new Tripartite Jobs Council reflects that workers and businesses already face disruption from AI and economic change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The newly announced Tripartite Jobs Council reflects that reality that workers and businesses are already facing disruption from AI and economic change.

sections.label: SWDA and CET connection
sections.summary: SWDA must connect continuing education and training to job transitions, employer recognition and labour market demand, or learning lacks a clear route.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, if SWDA is to succeed, it must not only support participation in CET.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It must ensure CET is much more closely connected to job transitions, employer recognition and actual labour market demand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Otherwise, we are asking people to invest time, effort and money into learning without giving them a clearer route forward and that would be deeply unfair.

sections.label: Merger towards upstream guidance
sections.summary: The merger moves beyond fragmented support towards upstream guidance, better triaging, stronger service integration and support before crisis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And this is where the merger in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It talks about moving beyond fragmented support towards upstream guidance, better triaging, stronger service integration and support that comes before crisis, not after.

sections.label: Existing career support tools
sections.summary: Singaporeans have MyCareersFuture and the Careers and Skills Passport, while e2i's NTUC AI Career Coach seeks more integrated career support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Today, Singaporeans already have Government tools, such as MyCareersFuture and the Careers and Skills Passport to support job search and career planning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the same time, e2i's NTUC AI Career Coach is trying to make career support more integrated and easier to use.

sections.label: Tripartite coordination with SWDA
sections.summary: An agency alone does not place workers, so tripartite coordination is essential, including SWDA working with the Tripartite Jobs Council.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But an agency alone does not place workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And that is why strong tripartite coordination remains essential, including how SWDA works alongside the newly announced Tripartite Jobs Council so that training, transformation and job transitions reinforce one another, because people do not experience policy in neat categories.

sections.label: Questions on SWDA success
sections.summary: Three questions ask how SWDA will move upstream, measure success beyond participation, and improve service experience within one or two years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, how will SWDA move upstream to close both the first-job gap for students and the transition gap for adult learners, so that pathways become clearer much earlier?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Second, how will SWDA measure success beyond participation numbers, including whether people are placed into suitable jobs, whether they stay, whether they progress and whether their wages improve over time?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Third, what concrete service experience should Singaporeans feel within the next one or two years in guidance, in matching and transition support that will show this merger is actually making the pathway much clearer.

sections.label: Private education institutes under two Ministries
sections.summary: Adult private education institutes established under clause 78 of the Bill will fall under MOE and MOM.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Adult private education institutes established under clause 78 of the Bill will be under the purview of two Ministries: MOE and MOM.

sections.label: WSG 2024 employment figures
sections.summary: WSG's annual report noted that in 2024, around 40,000 local workers secured employment via WSG and e2i career matching services.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: WSG's annual report noted that in 2024, around 40,000 local workers managed to secure employment via WSG and e2i's career matching services.

sections.label: SSG-funded course evaluation framework
sections.summary: SSG-funded courses are currently evaluated through the training quality and outcomes measurement framework, which surveys participants.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, SSG-funded courses are evaluated via the training quality and outcomes measurement framework, which surveys participants.

sections.label: Workers' Party SkillsFuture KPI calls
sections.summary: The Workers' Party manifesto calls for tracking and publishing KPIs on SkillsFuture and career coaching programmes' effectiveness, including take-up rate, employment duration and post-training placement.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party manifesto includes calls for the Government to track and publish clear KPIs on the effectiveness of SkillsFuture and career coaching programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Such data may include the take-up rate, duration of employment and post-training placement.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan 2030 employment target
sections.summary: The Enabling Masterplan 2030 aims for a 40% employment rate among PwDs by that year, but other factors must also be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, while the Enabling Masterplan 2030 aims to achieve a 40% employment rate among PwDs by that year, there are other factors to be considered as well.

sections.label: PwD employment rate and concerns
sections.summary: The employment rate for PwDs rose to 34.7% in 2025, but many PwDs say roles offered by employment support services do not meet their aspirations and skillsets.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Although the employment rate for PwDs has increased to 34.7% in 2025, many PwDs have expressed concerns that the roles offered to them by employment support services often do not meet their career aspirations and skillsets.

sections.label: PwD training barriers and closure
sections.summary: PwDs were affected by Mountbatten Vocational School's closure, and many cited accessibility issues and disability barriers in attending training programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Many PwDs were affected by the recent closure of Mountbatten Vocational School, which provides PwDs with higher support needs and avenue to pick up skills in preparation for a subsequent education at the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) or entry into the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For PwDs with lower support needs, many have cited difficulty participating in SkillsFuture courses due to accessibility issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is backed up by the 2024 Disability Trends report highlighting that 61.6% of PwDs noted that they found it difficult to attend training programmes due to barriers because of their disability.

sections.label: SkillsFuture website AI revamp
sections.summary: Reskilling includes revamping the SkillsFuture website with more focus on AI and a free six-month premium AI subscription for select AI courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the domain of reskilling, this includes revamping the SkillsFuture website with an increased focus on AI and offering participants of select AI courses, a free six-month premium AI subscription.

sections.label: SSG and WSG single board
sections.summary: The Bill brings SSG and WSG under a single Statutory Board, strengthening coherence across skills development, employment facilitation and career progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: By bringing together SSG and WSG under a single Statutory Board, this Bill strengthens coherence across skills development, employment facilitation and career progression.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model key pillar
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model remains a key pillar in these efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) remains a key pillar in our efforts.

sections.label: Align training with PWM ladders
sections.summary: The new agency is urged to align training pathways more closely with PWM job ladders so workers see skills upgrading leading to wage progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: First, I urge the new agency to align training pathways more closely with PWM job ladders, so that workers can clearly see how skills upgrading leads to wage progression.

sections.label: Flexi-Work grant support proposal
sections.summary: The new agency is asked to consider targeted support for flexible work arrangements, such as a Flexi-Work grant for modified roles, reduced hours or phased return-to-work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can the new agency consider introducing targeted support for flexible work arrangements, such as a "Flexi-Work" grant to encourage modified roles, reduced hours, or even phased return-to-work options?

sections.label: Judging success for workers
sections.summary: Success is judged by workers' lived experience: moving between jobs, skills upgrading leading to wage progression, and lower-wage workers' sustained livelihood improvements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Success will be judged by how well we improve the lived experience of workers – whether they can move with confidence between jobs, whether skills upgrading leads to real wage progression and whether lower-wage workers see sustained improvements in their livelihoods.

sections.label: Place-and-Train programme outcomes
sections.summary: WSG's Place-and-Train Career Conversion Programmes placed close to 18,000 mid-career Singaporeans between 2017 and 2022, with wages rising up to 6.5% by year four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: WSG's Place-and-Train Career Conversion Programmes are – by the Government's 2024 evaluation – a success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Close to 18,000 mid-career Singaporeans were placed between 2017 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Wages rose by up to 6.5% by year four.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme reach
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, offering a $4,000 top-up, reached only 28,000 of 1.2 million eligible citizens by end-2024, or 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On demand: the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme – the flagship of mid-career upskilling, offering a $4,000 top-up – had reached only 28,000 out of 1.2 million eligible citizens by end-2024, which is only 2%.

sections.label: France suspected fraud rise
sections.summary: France's financial intelligence unit TRACFIN recorded suspected fraud rising five-fold in a year, from €8 million in 2020 to €43 million in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: TRACFIN, France's financial intelligence unit, recorded a five-fold rise in suspected fraud in a single year, from €8 million in 2020 to €43 million in 2021.

sections.label: German apprentices' earnings and supports
sections.summary: German apprentices earn about 15% more than the untrained two decades after entry, with lower unemployment risk and faster re-employment, aided by wage compression and portable credentials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: German apprentices earn about 15% more than the untrained two decades after entry, with lower unemployment risk and faster re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, wage compression – sectoral bargaining that narrows pay differentials within a sector so rivals cannot simply poach trained workers at a premium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, portable credentials – standardised, externally certified occupational profiles, so a worker's skill is legible to the whole labour market and the worker is willing to invest their own time.

sections.label: Advanced Certificate coursework requirement
sections.summary: The Advanced Certificate in Learning and Performance requires 71 hours of coursework, screening out domain experts and screening in those with time to spare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Advanced Certificate in Learning and Performance requires 71 hours of coursework, screening out the domain experts we need and screening in those with time to spare.

sections.label: Teardown facilities at ITEs polytechnics
sections.summary: The speaker proposes physical teardown facilities at ITEs and polytechnics as a vertical curriculum from guided disassembly to design analysis to cost modelling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is no reason it cannot exist here as public infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose we establish physical teardown facilities at our ITEs and polytechnics – not as one-off workshops, but as a vertical curriculum progressing from guided disassembly to design analysis to cost modelling.

sections.label: ITRI example and Industrial Commons Rotation
sections.summary: The speaker cites ITRI staff moving into Taiwanese industry and proposes a statutory Industrial Commons Rotation seconding large-firm staff into SMEs with reciprocal flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) is the clearest example: between 1973 and 2008, 13,000 ITRI staff moved into Taiwanese industry, many of them seeding what became TSMC, UMC and the wider Hsinchu semiconductor cluster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To speed up the rate of knowledge diffusion, I also propose an Industrial Commons Rotation: a statutory obligation on large firms – Government-linked corporations and major anchor MNCs – to second mid-senior technical staff into SMEs within the same sectoral cluster for six- to 18-month rotations, with reciprocal SME-to-large-firm flows so the small firms' problem-solving feeds back into the larger firms' processes.

sections.label: Instructor industry attachment pilot
sections.summary: The speaker notes polytechnic and ITE industry attachments are discretionary and proposes a pilot of 12 months in industry per 60 months of teaching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Polytechnic and ITE instructors can currently take industry attachments as a form of voluntary continuing professional development, but the mechanism is discretionary, not structural.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose a pilot: 12 months in industry for every 60 months of teaching.

sections.label: Initial target and early 2026 support
sections.summary: The initial target was 250 individuals over two years, and about 120 had been supported by early 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The initial target was 250 individuals over two years; about 120 had been supported by early 2026.

sections.label: Expanding to 5,000-person cohort
sections.summary: The speaker proposes expanding the pilot by an order of magnitude to a 5,000-person annual cohort within five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, expand it by an order of magnitude – from a 250-person pilot to a 5,000-person annual cohort within five years.

sections.label: Support for Bill on SSG-WSG merger
sections.summary: The speaker says people want to know how SWDA will do better and rises to support the Bill because the SSG and WSG merger is not good policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They want to know how will SWDA do better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I rise to support this Bill because the merger of SSG and WSG is just not good policy.

sections.label: Reskilled worker salary tokenism
sections.summary: Hiring a reskilled worker at the same salary is tokenism, and the new agency should track time-to-placement, wage growth and job-fit rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hiring a reskilled worker at the same salary as before is not transformation; it is tokenism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the new agency to track and publish time-to-placement, wage growth post-training and job-fit rates.

sections.label: SSG-NTUC-FairPrice upskilling partnership
sections.summary: Through the SSG-NTUC-FairPrice Group partnership, 1,000 workers across their SME supplier network are being upskilled, lifting the ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through the SSG-NTUC-FairPrice Group partnership, 1,000 workers across their SME supplier network are being upskilled, lifting the entire ecosystem, not just one company.

sections.label: SWDA worker board representation
sections.summary: SWDA will make decisions shaping livelihoods and career paths, and the speaker asks whether workers will be represented at board level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SWDA will make decisions that directly shape livelihoods and career paths of hundreds of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask: will there be worker representation at the board level and not just through consultations but as part of the governance structure itself?

sections.label: ITE Work-Study Diploma growth
sections.summary: The ITE Work-Study Diploma grew to 45 courses and 1,600 trainees in 2025, and the new agency must amplify skills-based careers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ITE Work-Study Diploma has grown from four courses and 100 trainees to 45 courses and 1,600 trainees in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The new agency must amplify this, creating celebrated, visible pathway for skills-based careers with competitive wages and real advancement so that choosing skills over a degree is never seen as settling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The same agency that funds your course must connect you to a job that values those skills and tracks whether your wages have improved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Labour market data must ensure we never train workers for yesterday's economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The agency must stay ahead of industry shifts, and recalibrate constantly measuring success in real wages and real career growth.

sections.label: SSG and WSG merger chance
sections.summary: The merger of SSG and WSG gives the chance to build a single agency that transforms workers' lives, not just trains and places them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The merger of SSG and WSG gives us the chance to build something better: a single, powerful, compassionate agency that does not just create programmes to train and place workers but to transform their lives.

sections.label: SSG and WSG merger
sections.summary: The merger of SSG and WSG into a single agency is not just an administrative consolidation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The merger of SSG and WSG into a single agency is therefore not just an administrative consolidation.

sections.label: SkillsFuture pathway positioning
sections.summary: Asks how the new agency will position SkillsFuture as a pathway for sector entry, conversion or in-sector progression.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify how the new agency will position SkillsFuture as a pathway for sector entry and conversion or as a pathway for in sector progression?

sections.label: Defining and tracking success
sections.summary: Asks how the new agency will define and track success, including placement rates and progression for mid-career switches.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: And it takes a clear focus on outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I therefore seek clarification from the Minister on how the new agency will define and track success.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For example, will the agency track placement rates within six to 12 months?

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: And progression over time, especially for mid-career switches?

sections.label: Accessible training for vulnerable workers
sections.summary: Asks how the new agency will keep training pathways accessible and relevant for workers facing greater barriers, and track outcomes across workforce segments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The ability to upgrade while in employment is not available to all.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: While we have encouraged employers to send workers for training, companies may still prioritise those who are already seen as higher potential.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: More vulnerable workers can be overlooked or sidelined and this becomes a compounding disadvantage when they eventually face displacement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: These realities limit their capacity to train after hours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I would therefore ask the Minister how the new agency will ensure that these training pathways remain accessible and relevant to these groups I have mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: How will support be sufficiently intensive to those who face greater barriers?

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: And how will outcomes be tracked, not just in aggregate, but across different segments of the workforce?

sections.label: Merger of SSG and WSG
sections.summary: Welcomes the merger of SSG and WSG to form SWDA, aligning training with labour market needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Like many other Members of this House, I welcome the merger of the SSG and WSG agencies to form SWDA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The merits of this merger are clear: it will align training closely with labour market needs, strengthening the nexus between training, employability and employment outcomes.

sections.label: MOM coordination with MOE
sections.summary: Asks how MOM will coordinate with MOE to give SWDA direction on CET and sustain IHLs as lifelong learning institutions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the new agency is under MOM, how will it ensure that this momentum is not lost, and that the IHLs will continue to develop as institutions of lifelong learning?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, how will MOM coordinate with MOE to provide direction to SWDA on CET?

sections.label: Returns on training investment
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry will assess the returns on investment in training.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, and this is critical, could the Ministry share how it will assess the returns on investment in training.

sections.label: Skills-first employment practices
sections.summary: Skills-first practices recognise skills rather than academic credentials for recruitment and advancement, and the speaker asks whether the new agency will champion them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Embedding capabilities within organisations is key, as job redesign and reskilling are not a one-off exercise, but something that enterprises and organisations will have to go through repeatedly as technology continually reshapes work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Skills-first employment practices will be critical in the new ecosystem of learning and work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means recognising skills rather than just academic credentials as the primary currency for recruitment, career development and advancement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This provides more mobility for workers, so that their career paths are not constrained by their past educational backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For these reasons, skills-first practices are important for job market efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to ask whether the new agency will continue to champion skills-first employment practices and what more can be done to facilitate and accelerate that adoption of skills-first practices by employers, workers and training providers.

sections.label: Lifelong education and training shift
sections.summary: The integrated SWDA reflects a shift from education only before a job towards continuing education and training throughout life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The new integrated SWDA reflects two important generational shifts for our system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, a shift from focusing on education only before getting a job, towards continuing education and training throughout the lifetime.

sections.label: Demand-led model shift
sections.summary: The second shift is from a supply-driven model to a demand-led model closer to employers and the marketplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The second shift is a shift from a supply-driven model that is less likely to lead to a job, to a demand-led model, which is closer to the employers and to the marketplace.

sections.label: SWDA focus and resources
sections.summary: The speaker hopes SWDA under MOM will have renewed focus and more resources for enterprise-led on-the-job training and accredited training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, perhaps the political officeholder at MOE and MOM can also have a role at NTUC: three-in-one, like the coffee, and we need to give a caffeine boost to our skills and workforce development initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that SWDA under MOM will have renewed focus and an increase in resources to support enterprise-led on-the-job training as well as training only if it is accredited by trade associations or our unions.

sections.label: Support for long-term jobseekers
sections.summary: Anyone looking for a job for more than six months, including recent graduates, should qualify for the same support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Anyone looking for a job for more than six months, even a recent graduate, should qualify for the same support.

sections.label: Right incentives for training
sections.summary: The right incentives should give training providers, employers and employees better employment, training and job outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The right incentives, so that any training provider knows that we are looking for good long term employment outcomes and not just a good course feedback form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The right incentives, so that employers are able to train more workers to acquire the right skills and stay employable, instead of expecting to only hire workers after they are fully trained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And most importantly, the right incentives, so that employees have greater assurance that if they put in effort to find a job or to go for training, they will have a better chance of growing with a good job.

sections.label: SSG and WSG merger
sections.summary: The SSG and WSG merger matters for job-skills ecosystems, linking training and skills to relevant jobs and careers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The merger of SSG and WSG is a relevant one in our job-skills ecosystems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I think the more important thing is to make sure that the input, the training and the skills and acquisitions, link directly to the output which are relevant jobs and a high-value career.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recognition of the training or the skills is the currency of the labour market.

sections.label: SWDA aligning skills frameworks
sections.summary: If SWDA aligns skills frameworks with professional institutions' accreditation standards, lifelong learning becomes lifelong career advancement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If SWDA can align our skills frameworks with the accreditation standards of these professional institutions, then we will have turned "lifelong learning" into "lifelong career advancement".

sections.label: Professional institutions recognising courses
sections.summary: Course developers must involve professional institutions to recognise courses and experience, so developed skills match industry rewards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Which means that, when they are developing the modules or the courses, they must make sure that the professional institutions are involved and can recognise such courses and also the experiences that are being acquired.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, we must ensure that the skills we develop are the same skills that the industry rewards.

sections.label: New SWDA macro mission
sections.summary: The new SWDA's macro mission dovetails with the outlined aims, showing potential synergy for workers' and employers' challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The macro mission of the new SWDA dovetails with what I have outlined, and one can clearly see the potential for great synergy in addressing the challenges faced by both workers and employers.

sections.label: Reviewing SkillsFuture credit caps
sections.summary: The $4,000 mid-career top-up may not suffice, so SkillsFuture credit caps should be reviewed to give greater support to committed upgraders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The $4,000 mid-career top-up provides a meaningful baseline, but for these individuals, it may not be enough.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We should review our approach to SkillsFuture credit caps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Instead of a one-size fits-all approach, we should consider providing greater support to those who demonstrate a commitment to continuous upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: By doing so, we encourage deeper, more purposeful learning and better support workers who take charge of their career health, and strive to remain relevant and competitive.

sections.label: WDA restructured into two agencies
sections.summary: In 2016 WDA was restructured into SSG, for skills training, CET and SkillsFuture policy, and WSG, for job design, coaching and matching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2016, WDA was restructured into two agencies – SSG, which focuses on skills training, CET and SkillsFuture policy; and WSG, which focuses on job design, career coaching and job matching.

sections.label: Training, jobs and career alignment
sections.summary: The core issue is a lack of alignment between training, jobs and career progression, making the shift to an integrated train-for-jobs model under SWDA timely and necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, the core issue is a lack of alignment between training, jobs and career progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And this is precisely why the shift towards an integrated "train-for-jobs" model under SWDA is both timely and necessary.

sections.label: Outcome-based funding for training providers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes tying training provider funding to career outcomes like job placement, transitions and wage growth, with part possibly deferred until achieved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The real measure of success is whether training improves a person's working life, whether training improves their life as a whole, whether it leads to employment, enables a career transition or results in wage progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would therefore propose a move towards a more explicit outcome-based funding model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under this approach, funding for training providers is tied to tangible career outcomes, such as job placement, successful transitions and wage growth, with part of the funding possibly deferred until these outcomes are achieved.

sections.label: SkillsFuture certifications unevenly valued
sections.summary: SkillsFuture certifications may not be consistently valued like IHL qualifications due to uneven quality, and some employers may not rely on them as job readiness indicators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, as I said before, these certifications are possibly not consistently valued in the same way as qualifications from our IHLs, due to uneven quality, and some employers might not even be prepared to rely on SkillsFuture certifications as indicators of job readiness.

sections.label: Tier One and Tier Two training
sections.summary: Tier One focuses on job-linked training with stronger subsidies tied to employment outcomes, while Tier Two could support personal enrichment with limited subsidies and mandatory co-payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With Tier One focusing on job-linked training, with stronger subsidies tied to clear employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Tier Two, perhaps, could support personal enrichment, where individuals may still use their SkillsFuture credits, but with limited or no additional subsidies and with a mandatory co-payment requirement.

sections.label: SWDA establishment creates opportunity
sections.summary: The establishment of SWDA creates an opportunity to address this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The establishment of SWDA creates an opportunity to address this.

sections.label: Further tranche of SkillsFuture credit
sections.summary: Over a million Singaporeans have used their initial SkillsFuture credits, so a further carefully calibrated tranche aligned with an outcome-based approach is timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we strengthen this system, Sir, we should recognise that more than a million Singaporeans have already utilised their initial SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If lifelong learning is to remain a national strategy, it is timely to consider a further tranche of SkillsFuture credit, carefully calibrated and aligned with an outcome-based approach.

sections.label: Skills and jobs under SWDA
sections.summary: The new SWDA brings skills and jobs under one roof to help Singaporeans navigate a changing labour market through a more integrated system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Success is no longer simply climbing higher in a straight line but about knowing where to move next, which skills to build, how to switch routes entirely and being able to try again after falling from the rock wall.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It supports Singaporeans in navigating a changing labour market by bringing skills and jobs under one roof through a new SWDA, so that Singaporeans experience a more integrated and truly "no wrong door" system.

sections.label: Resident's mid-career transition difficulty
sections.summary: A resident completed a SkillsFuture Career Transition programme course in 2025 but received no job offers despite certifications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A resident wrote to me, just today, sharing his difficult mid-career transition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: He completed a desktop support engineering course under the SkillsFuture Career Transition programme in 2025 to transition into an entry-level IT role in the hopes of improving his employment prospects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The training provider also said that they would support job placement efforts, but entry-level opportunities in this field are limited, competition is stiff, the market for such roles is niche and many employers prioritise candidates with relevant experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Thus, despite acquiring the relevant certifications, he has not received any job offers.

sections.label: Agency's anticipatory role with AI
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government sees the agency working with industry bodies to prepare training and transition pathways before major disruptions, especially AI-driven changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Does the Government see the agency playing a concretely anticipatory role, working with industry bodies to prepare training and transition pathways before major disruptions occur, especially since AI drives structural workforce changes that may lead to substantial layoffs and job obsolescence.

sections.label: Community outreach and flexible training models
sections.summary: The question asks how the new agency will work with the community and design flexible training models, modular learning and micro-credentials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Bishan East-Sin Ming, we have a Career Navigators programme, where volunteers work closely with e2i and journey alongside jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Government share how the new agency will work with the community to proactively identify and support these groups, perhaps through neighbourhood-based outreach or peer mentors?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How will we design flexible training models that respect caregiving responsibilities, health conditions and different learning needs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And can we make more space for a modular learning and micro-credentials that still add up to meaningful progression, so that those who cannot commit to a long qualification do not feel shut out.

sections.label: Hopes for deeper transformation
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the new SWDA will lead toward a deeper transformation in the next phase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For the next phase, I hope the new SWDA will lead us toward a deeper transformation.

sections.label: Support for SWDA Bill intention
sections.summary: The speaker rises in support of the intention behind the new SWDA to bring skills, careers and workforce support into a more coherent system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And this is precisely why this Bill matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I rise in support of the intention behind the new SWDA to bring skills, careers and workforce support together into a more coherent and coordinated system.

sections.label: SSG WSG coordination gaps
sections.summary: Asks what specific coordination gaps or overlaps remain if SSG and WSG have largely achieved their intended objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If SSG and WSG have largely achieved their intended objectives, then what specific coordination gaps or overlaps remain today?

sections.label: Clause 5(3) no enforceable duty
sections.summary: Clause 5(3) makes clear that these functions do not create an enforceable duty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 5(3) makes clear that these functions do not create an enforceable duty.

sections.label: Participation versus employment outcomes
sections.summary: Asks whether success is programme participation or return to work, age, wage and duration, and whether to move to place-and-train.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is it participation in programmes, or is it how quickly someone returns to work, at what age and what wage, and for how long they remain employed?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: More fundamentally, should we move decisively towards a place-and-train model, where employment is secured upfront and training follows rather than asking residents to train first without a clear job pathway?

sections.label: Training leading to jobs
sections.summary: Asks whether SWDA will track whether training leads to jobs and assess providers on placement rates, wage outcomes and retention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A course that is completed but does not improve employability is not a success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, will SWDA track whether training actually leads to jobs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will providers be assessed based on placement rates, wage outcomes and retention?

sections.label: Outcome-based reporting and funding
sections.summary: Suggests outcome-based reporting by programme type, disclosure of placement and wage outcomes, and funding tied to sustained employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To strengthen this pillar, I suggest first, having outcome-based reporting by programme type; second, disclosure of placement and wage outcomes; and third, funding tied to sustained employment, not just completion.

sections.label: Partner roles and complaints pathway
sections.summary: Asks whether they will be delivery, referral or advisory partners and whether residents will have a single complaints and appeals pathway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will they be delivery partners, referral partners or advisory partners?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And critically, will residents have a single complaints and appeals pathway?

sections.label: SWDA functions beyond SSG WSG
sections.summary: Asks what new thrusts the SWDA's functions under clause 5 add beyond existing SSG and WSG functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Even after they were housed under different Agencies, SSG and WSG, they collaborate to work together to build a robust and integrated jobs and skills ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
